title: Negative argument from Scripture — reject what lacks Scriptural foundation
source_text: XXXVII. Atque hinc est quod a sacrae Scripturae authoritate negative argumentamur. Quandoquidem enim eorum quae Deus per Prophetas & Apostolos revelavit, nihil omnino certi ad nos pervenit, praeter ea quae ipsi divinitus scripto mandarunt, ut aliquid rejiciamus tanquam ad fidem non pertinens, satis est ut in Scriptura fundamentum non habeat, nec possit ex ea probari & deduci.
pass_a_gloss: And hence it is that we argue negatively from the authority of sacred Scripture. For since of those things which God revealed through the Prophets and Apostles nothing at all certain has come down to us except those which they themselves by divine command committed to writing, in order that we may reject something as not pertaining to faith, it is enough that it does not have a foundation in Scripture, and cannot be proved and deduced from it.
pass_b_english: Hence we argue negatively from Scripture's authority.

Of what God revealed through the Prophets and Apostles, nothing certain has reached us except what they themselves divinely committed to writing. To reject something as not belonging to faith, it is enough that it has no foundation in Scripture and cannot be proved or drawn from it.

choices.why: Classic Reformed negative use of sola Scriptura.
Divine charge to write, not mere habit.
